summary: History of vaccine refusal from the first smallpox vaccines and 19th-century anti-vaccination leagues in Britain and the US to Andrew Wakefield's fraudulent MMR study and Dr. Bob Sears's alternative schedules, linked to measles outbreaks.

evidence.note: Jenner presents the cowpox vaccine in 1796, the starting point of the story
Boston doctors and clergy form the first anti-vaccination society in 1798
Stockholm vaccine refusal and the 1874 epidemic get a segment
Leicester mass march, Royal Commission and conscience clause in Britain
smallpox framed as a Black disease; racist quarantines and enforcement in the US South
Little edits The Liberator and later wins anti-compulsion laws in Michigan
homeopath and health-nut doctors in the movement; Pfeiffer catches smallpox after a challenge
Jacobson v. Massachusetts 1905 ends the first American movement
Wakefield patents tests and a single measles vaccine to profit from his MMR claims
Vaxxed documentary and Infowars appearances push a CDC cover-up claim
Sears placed on probation by the California medical board in 2018
2019 Clark County measles outbreak tied to modern vaccine refusal

notes: Primary subject is the movement, so roles stay empty and Wakefield and Sears are secondary despite having a part each. Transcript spells her Laura Little; historical name is Lora Little. Sears birth year left null (unsure). Main span 1798-2018 because the story narrates both the 19th-century movement and the modern revival. Medical-malpractice considered for Wakefield's birthday-party blood draws but left out.
